edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Protein intake around 1.2 g/kg/day is plausibly linked to Muscle mass through mechanisms that fit its exposure class and target tissue, but the exact pathway depends on dose, timing, and baseline vulnerability. The best interpretation is usually that it changes the biologic setting in which Muscle mass develops rather than acting as a single on-off switch.
edges.summary: Protein intake around 1.2 g/kg/day appears tied to better muscle mass in community-dwelling older adults mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. In older adults, the signal is usually about avoiding under-protein intake rather than proving that ever-higher protein doses keep adding benefit.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
